paragraphs: Auxiliary sensors can help recover detail from dark video, but enhancement systems often depend on those sensors still being available when deployed. AnyMod-LLVE introduces AMNet to make that dependence more flexible. Its goal is to enhance low-light RGB video across different combinations of available auxiliary inputs, including situations where those inputs are missing.

The central component learns correspondences between RGB images and auxiliary modalities through spatial and spectral processing controlled by gates. When an auxiliary input is absent, the translator produces an implicit representation of the information it would contribute. The framework also uses large-scale pretraining on RGB-only data augmented with synthetic auxiliary modalities, giving it additional opportunities to learn relationships across inputs.

The reported experiments show that AMNet handles arbitrary inference-time modality combinations and performs better under missing-modality conditions. The practical contribution is a shared enhancement framework whose operation can adapt to available inputs. Its learned auxiliary representations support enhancement without requiring every modality used to establish cross-modal correspondences to remain available during inference.
icml-2026-anymod-llve-low-light-video-en.tldr: AMNet enhances low-light video with flexible sensor inputs by learning implicit auxiliary representations for missing modalities.

paragraphs: Reaching a distant goal can depend on passing through a few difficult transitions between regions. This paper makes those bottlenecks the organizing principle for learning from an offline dataset. Instead of selecting intermediate goals by elapsed time or short-range value estimates, it explicitly searches for states that indicate where the agent should pass next.

The method applies Laplacian spectral clustering to identify regions and their boundaries. Recorded trajectories crossing those boundaries supply candidate keypoints. Representative keypoints become nodes in a directed reachability graph, which guides high-level decisions. A replaceable low-level controller carries out the shorter movements between selected bottleneck states.

The theoretical justification assumes a standard metastable decomposition of the state space. Under that assumption, bottleneck routing gives an approximately optimal next subgoal for hitting time, and spectral information recovers bottlenecks with high overlap. Experiments across D4RL and OGBench report state-of-the-art performance, including 96.5% on AntMaze and 84.7% on Franka-Kitchen. These results support bottlenecks as useful planning landmarks across the evaluated navigation, manipulation, and dataset settings.
icml-2026-bottleneck-guided-spectral-sub.tldr: Spectral clustering identifies bottleneck states that guide offline goal-conditioned agents through useful intermediate goals.

paragraphs: Graph contrastive learning builds representations without supervised labels, but its training choices can distort the relationships it should preserve. Random graph changes may alter meaning, while rigid one-to-one sampling can mix different classes and scatter members of the same class. CL-GCL addresses these problems by organizing learning around graph structure and local geometry.

The framework uses graph coarsening to represent communities, preserving structural meaning at a broader scale. It also uses manifold learning to capture local geometric relationships without expensive pairwise distance calculations. Together, these components fit the neighborhood aggregation used by graph convolutional networks, strengthen structural consistency, and eliminate the negative-sampling bias identified in the paper.

The authors prove that the resulting objective approximates a node-level contrastive loss under mild conditions. This connects the lighter formulation to the finer-grained learning objective it aims to replace. Experiments report consistent gains in both accuracy and efficiency over state-of-the-art graph contrastive methods, suggesting that preserving meaningful structure can improve representation quality while also reducing computational burden.
icml-2026-cl-gcl-comprehensive-and-light.tldr: CL-GCL combines community representations and local geometry to improve graph contrastive learning accuracy and efficiency.

paragraphs: Scene graphs describe a scene through entities and their relationships, but those relationships can reflect accidental patterns specific to a training environment. Such patterns become unreliable when the environment changes. CURVE addresses this by seeking a sparse relationship structure that remains stable across domains, using uncertainty to help determine which relations deserve less emphasis.

The framework combines variational uncertainty modeling with structural regularization guided by that uncertainty. Relations with high variation tied to particular environments are suppressed. A prototype-conditioned debiasing component further separates stable interaction dynamics from environment-dependent variation. The approach is inspired by causal reasoning and uses that perspective to organize representation learning around interactions that transfer more reliably.

The authors evaluate CURVE through zero-shot transfer and adaptation from simulation to reality with little data. They report domain-stable sparse graph structures and reliable uncertainty estimates that support risk prediction under distribution shifts. The findings connect two useful outcomes: more transferable scene representations and uncertainty information that helps assess risk when observations differ from the training environment.
icml-2026-curve-learning-causality-inspi.tldr: CURVE uses uncertainty-guided regularization to learn sparse scene relationships that transfer more reliably across environments.

paragraphs: Vision-language-action policies translate images and instructions into robot behavior. This paper changes how their actions are decoded: action chunks are discretized and progressively refined by discrete diffusion within the same transformer backbone. Keeping action generation inside that backbone is intended to preserve pretrained visual and language knowledge while supporting a unified architecture.

Decoding follows confidence rather than a fixed left-to-right order. The model resolves action elements it is confident about first, then handles more difficult elements. Secondary re-masking lets it revisit uncertain predictions, providing another opportunity to correct errors. The design also supports parallel decoding and improves efficiency.

Reported results include 96.4% average success on LIBERO, 71.2% visual matching on SimplerEnv-Fractal, and 54.2% overall on SimplerEnv-Bridge. In LIBERO-Goal distribution-shift tests, language degradation is 0.8% versus 8.0% for parallel decoding, while vision degradation is 20.4% versus 29.0% for continuous diffusion. These comparisons support improved retention of pretrained capabilities in the evaluated settings. Two real-robot evaluations on AgileX Cobot Magic further demonstrate the method's effectiveness.
icml-2026-discrete-diffusion-vla-bringin.tldr: Discrete Diffusion VLA refines robot action tokens inside a unified transformer, using confidence-based decoding and re-masking for error correction.

paragraphs: Diffusion language models process token blocks in parallel, yet only a small fraction of their tokens may be ready for decoding at a given refinement step. The paper identifies this mismatch as a source of wasted computation. Processing an entire block does not necessarily translate into useful progress across the entire block.

FOCUS uses an observed correlation between attention-derived token importance and the probability that a token can be decoded. Its inference system dynamically concentrates computation on decodable tokens and evicts non-decodable ones from ongoing computation. This allocation increases the effective batch size and helps relieve the compute bottleneck, enabling higher throughput.

In large-batch evaluations, FOCUS achieves up to 3.52 times the throughput of LMDeploy while maintaining or improving generation quality across multiple benchmarks. The result is a maximum reported improvement in that setting, rather than a fixed speedup for every workload. The contribution is an inference-system strategy that makes block-parallel diffusion more productive by matching computational attention to where decoding progress is currently possible.
icml-2026-focus-dllms-know-how-to-tame-t.tldr: FOCUS accelerates diffusion language model inference by concentrating computation on tokens likely to be decodable at each step.

paragraphs: Discretizing physical equations produces sparse linear systems that require accurate numerical solutions. Neural methods can accelerate this work, but their accuracy and generalization may be insufficient, and hybrid solvers can stall as their remaining errors change. G-RANS addresses this by making each learned correction depend on the current residual, which measures how far the current solution is from satisfying the system.

The solver maps that residual onto the matrix graph and generates correction subspaces at multiple scales. A differentiable projection then computes updates within those subspaces. Training is fully self-supervised and progressively incorporates residual distributions from multiple stages, preparing the model for the changing errors encountered during iteration.

Tests cover sparse finite-element systems from Poisson, advection-diffusion, reaction-diffusion, and Helmholtz equations. G-RANS shows robustness to coefficient shifts up to ±70% and strong transfer across equations. It reaches relative residuals around 10^-5 and requires two to four times less wall-clock time than classical Krylov solvers to reach the same target residual in the reported experiments.
icml-2026-g-rans-generalizable-residual-.tldr: G-RANS learns residual-dependent correction spaces to solve sparse physical systems accurately and faster in the reported evaluations.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning policies can produce rapid oscillations in their control signals, creating problems for physical stability and safety. Predicting whole action sequences can smooth behavior, but increases the policy's output size with the prediction horizon. Dual-Window Smoothing instead promotes coherence over time while keeping the original action-space size and supporting step-wise interaction.

Its execution window deterministically modulates actions to make physical execution smoother. A separate value window aligns temporal-difference targets over the horizon, addressing critic bias introduced by open-loop execution. A lightweight actor regularizer also penalizes first-order differences between actions to encourage continuity. These mechanisms connect smooth execution with the learning signals used to evaluate and improve the policy.

Experiments on the DeepMind Control Suite and industrial energy management tasks report improvements over state-of-the-art baselines. In the evaluated vision-based autonomous driving tasks, the method produces smoother control, reduced jitter, safer behavior, and a 100% success rate. These findings support implicit action chunking as a way to obtain temporally coherent control without expanding policy outputs into fixed-horizon trajectories.
icml-2026-implicit-action-chunking-for-s.tldr: Dual-Window Smoothing improves control continuity by coordinating action execution and value learning without enlarging the action space.

paragraphs: LaViD investigates whether a language-only model can teach useful conceptual distinctions to a vision-only model. The teacher never needs to inspect images. Instead, the framework draws on knowledge acquired through text pretraining and converts it into supervision that helps the visual student distinguish fine-grained classes, without relying on paired multimodal data.

The language model generates multiple-choice questions about semantic differences between visual classes. Each class receives a soft label distribution over these questions, forming a conceptual signature. An auxiliary distillation loss uses these signatures to guide student training. This gives the student information about relationships and distinctions among classes beyond their individual class labels.

Across multiple fine-grained benchmarks, LaViD consistently outperforms MaKD, which distills knowledge from vision-language models. It also matches or exceeds the visual distillation methods DKD and MLKD, with further improvements from logit standardization. On Waterbirds, improved worst-group accuracy supports greater robustness to spurious correlations. The findings show that conceptual supervision from a language-only teacher can transfer usefully into visual recognition.
icml-2026-large-language-model-teaches-v.tldr: LaViD turns a language model's conceptual questions into supervision that improves fine-grained visual recognition and robustness.

paragraphs: Protein generation must balance plausible sequences with diversity, while retaining membership in a desired family. LineageFlow starts from the observation that uniform or masked-token noise discards evolutionary constraints at individual sequence positions. Reconstructing those constraints from scratch can weaken family control and foldability, so the method begins with a more informative starting point.

Its flow-matching model operates on amino-acid probability distributions and initializes generation from lineage priors obtained through ancestral sequence reconstruction. Generation therefore becomes structured mutation of an evolved scaffold. The paper also introduces rerouting: one intermediate mutate-select-amplify intervention that steers sampling toward an objective without requiring predictor guidance at every step.

Across diverse families, generated sequences approach held-out natural sequences in family validity and improve predicted structural confidence over uniform- and mask-initialized baselines. They retain substantial novelty and diversity within families, and the reported results even surpass a large pretrained baseline trained on considerably more data. Rerouting further improves plausibility, including in a zero-shot enzyme-generation case study. The structural-confidence findings concern predictions.
icml-2026-lineageflow-flow-matching-for-.tldr: LineageFlow generates diverse, family-consistent protein sequences by starting flow matching from reconstructed evolutionary priors.

paragraphs: Training directly with low-precision weights can save resources, but rounding can prevent an optimizer from changing a weight at all. This is especially problematic for large weight magnitudes, where representable values are spaced farther apart. The paper identifies this stalled progress as a key failure mode when high-precision weight copies are not retained.

M+Adam combines two complementary update mechanisms. Additive updates handle small magnitudes and changes of sign, where multiplicative methods can struggle. Multiplicative updates maintain progress at larger magnitudes when rounding would erase additive steps. The combination addresses weaknesses in each update type by assigning them complementary roles in low-precision optimization.

The authors prove monotone descent under standard smoothness assumptions. Their experiments cover LLaMA-style pretraining with 60 million to one billion parameters and budgets from one to eight times Chinchilla, using only BF16, FP8, or FP4 master weights. M+Adam consistently improves training across those reported settings. The theoretical result remains conditional on its assumptions, while the experiments show the benefit of combining update types across several precision and scale choices.
icml-2026-m-adam-low-precision-training-.tldr: M+Adam combines additive and multiplicative updates to prevent complementary rounding-related failures in low-precision training.

paragraphs: Language models may enforce safety more effectively in high-resource languages than in low-resource ones. This paper seeks to transfer existing safety capabilities across languages without the cost of multilingual fine-tuning or reinforcement learning from human feedback. Its starting observation is that safety capabilities are concentrated in a sparse set of neurons.

The method formulates alignment as a constrained linear transformation and derives a closed-form weight edit. Harmful representations from low-resource languages are mapped toward the safety subspaces associated with high-resource languages. A null-space projection constraint is used to preserve general utility. The resulting procedure is training-free, using a single data-efficient calculation rather than an iterative training process.

Experiments span eight languages and models from the Llama-3 and Qwen-2.5 families. The authors report substantially reduced attack success rates in low-resource languages with negligible effects on general reasoning. The findings support targeted weight editing as a computationally economical way to reduce the measured language gap in safety, while retaining the capabilities evaluated alongside it.
icml-2026-multilingual-safety-alignment-.tldr: A closed-form edit to sparse safety-related weights reduces multilingual safety disparities without iterative training.

paragraphs: Simulated depth measurements often fail to reproduce the varied errors of physical sensors, making transfer to real robots difficult. PRISM separates two kinds of noise that a single black-box model can obscure: sensing invalidation, where a valid measurement is unavailable, and measurement inaccuracy, where a reading exists but is wrong. This separation enables treatment tied to their different physical origins.

The three-part framework distills features from a 3D visual foundation model to supply spatial and semantic information for physics-based reasoning. It also addresses the rarity and imbalance of invalidation regions through supervision at multiple scales. Positive-weighted objectives and dynamic hard-example mining that preserves positive examples help the model delineate these artifacts precisely.

The reported benchmarks show state-of-the-art fidelity in synthesized noisy depth. Downstream robotic experiments achieve an average real-world success rate of 92.1%, improving substantially over monolithic noise-modeling baselines. Together, these findings connect a more physically differentiated sensor model with both more realistic synthetic depth and improved performance in the evaluated robot tasks.
icml-2026-prism-learning-realistic-depth.tldr: PRISM models missing and inaccurate depth readings separately to improve sensor-noise synthesis and sim-to-real robotic performance.

paragraphs: RealisMotion aims to make four parts of human video generation independently controllable: the person, the background, the path of movement, and the action being performed. Separating these elements allows them to be recombined more flexibly. The framework explicitly distinguishes motion from appearance, the subject from the surroundings, and action patterns from trajectories.

Motion editing takes place in a ground-aware 3D coordinate system. Edited 2D trajectories are converted into 3D using focal-length calibration and coordinate transformations, followed by adjustments to speed and orientation. Actions come from a motion bank or a text-to-motion method. This creates motion controls that account for movement through world space.

A text-to-video diffusion transformer then receives each control through a distinct mechanism: subject tokens participate in full attention, background information is concatenated along channels, and motion signals are added. Experiments on benchmark datasets and real-world cases report state-of-the-art element-wise controllability and overall video quality. The results support flexible composition of the evaluated elements, while the broader vision of arbitrary people, actions, and places remains a possibility enabled by the design.
icml-2026-realismotion-decomposed-human-.tldr: RealisMotion separates subject, background, trajectory, and action controls to generate human videos with editable motion in 3D world space.

paragraphs: REALISTA studies whether meaning-preserving rephrasings of ordinary prompts can induce language models to hallucinate. The task is framed as constrained optimization: adversarial prompts should remain coherent and semantically equivalent to their benign originals. This makes the evaluation about reliability under realistic wording changes, rather than arbitrary changes to the user's request.

Existing discrete attacks search a limited collection of rephrasings, while continuous latent-space attacks can explore more broadly but may decode into invalid paraphrases. REALISTA builds a dictionary specific to each input, with editing directions corresponding to coherent, equivalent rephrasings. It then optimizes continuous combinations of those directions in latent space, connecting flexible search with a structure grounded in valid edits.

Experiments on open-source language models show performance that is superior or comparable to state-of-the-art realistic attacks. The method also succeeds against large reasoning models in free-form response settings where previous realistic attacks fail. These findings expose reliability weaknesses that can remain hidden when evaluation covers only a narrower set of semantically equivalent prompts.
icml-2026-realista-realistic-latent-adve.tldr: REALISTA searches continuous combinations of valid rephrasing directions to find realistic prompts that elicit hallucinations.

paragraphs: Editing recorded driving scenes can expand the scenarios available for evaluating autonomous systems without collecting every scenario on the road. SceneDirector tackles simultaneous editing of objects and the ego vehicle's trajectory. This requires both flexible visual generation and precise spatial control, which the framework connects through explicit geometry and learned generative information.

LiDAR-guided depth completion constructs dense scene geometry, and editable 3D assets join it in a unified geometric scaffold. Separately, the source video is encoded into a static texture bank that supplies appearance context. The scaffold describes the scene's structure, while the bank provides visual information for rendering the edited scene.

Mask-gated reference attention coordinates these components using a measure of geometric uncertainty. It preserves geometry judged reliable and adaptively introduces texture information for semantic refinement. Evaluations report better controllability and visual quality than state-of-the-art methods. The contribution is a mechanism for coordinating spatial constraints with appearance generation, supporting joint scene and trajectory edits within one diffusion-based framework.
icml-2026-scenedirector-bridging-explici.tldr: SceneDirector combines a 3D geometric scaffold with source-video textures to jointly edit driving-scene objects and ego trajectories.

paragraphs: Spiking neural networks use sparse, event-driven activity, offering a route to efficient computation. Building multimodal transformers with them is difficult because deep spiking layers can train unstably and conventional dense softmax attention does not fit spike-based communication well. SMM Transformer addresses these issues alongside the need to combine information from multiple modalities.

The framework introduces a parallel leaky integrate-and-fire neuron with learnable parameters across multiple stages, paired with a tailored training algorithm to stabilize learning. A spike-driven attention approximation includes a lightweight self-compensation branch. A spiking mixture-of-experts module then handles modality-aware fusion, bringing training, attention, and multimodal integration into a shared design.

Across visual and multimodal benchmarks, SMM Transformer reaches accuracy competitive with conventional artificial neural network baselines. The attention module's estimated compute energy falls by up to 97% under a standard multiply-accumulate versus accumulate cost model. This is a modeled saving for the attention component, rather than a measured whole-system energy reduction. The findings support the feasibility of combining competitive task performance with substantially cheaper attention computation in the evaluated framework.
icml-2026-smm-transformer-leveraging-spi.tldr: SMM Transformer combines stable spiking training, spike-based attention, and modality-aware experts with competitive accuracy and lower estimated attention energy.

paragraphs: Handwriting images contain large background regions, and many positions along a text line contribute mostly blanks. Spike-HTR uses both imbalances to organize a hybrid spiking recognizer. It controls the number of spiking timesteps and the number of horizontal positions sent into the deeper sequence-processing component, addressing two distinct sources of computation.

InkCoder turns a static image into a coarse-to-fine stream. Early timesteps emphasize broad stroke regions, while later ones highlight sharper details, making the image suitable for short spiking inference. A CTC-guided length reducer retains likely character positions and uncertain positions, while compressing long blank-dominated stretches before deep sequence mixing.

With two spiking timesteps, training only on target data, and decoding without language models or lexicons, the system reports validation/test character error rates of 3.5/5.4 on IAM, 2.3/2.5 on LAM, and 4.2/3.9 on READ2016. These results establish the reported recognition performance under those specific training and decoding conditions. The approach combines selective spatial processing with a short temporal representation of the image.
icml-2026-spike-htr-spiking-neural-trans.tldr: Spike-HTR recognizes handwriting using a two-step coarse-to-fine spiking input and selective compression of blank-heavy sequence regions.

paragraphs: SpikingLM addresses two barriers to deep spiking language models. Inactive neurons can weaken gradients and make training ineffective. Meanwhile, removing softmax to save energy reduces competition among tokens, making it harder to select the most relevant ones. The framework introduces separate mechanisms for preserving trainability and restoring selective attention.

Distribution-aware scaling moves linear-layer outputs into a range that encourages neuron activation, reducing dead neurons and stabilizing gradient propagation. Its scaling parameters can be folded into preceding linear layers, so they add no inference overhead. Spike2Max restores a winner-takes-all mechanism through base-2 exponentiation and max-subtraction, using hardware-efficient bit shifts.

The paper reports that Spike2Max consumes over 95% less energy than softmax. At the model level, experiments report a 57.9% energy reduction and state-of-the-art performance on GLUE. These are separate component and model results. Together, they support the paper's proposed route toward energy-efficient language modeling: keep deep spiking networks active during training while retaining the token competition needed for useful language representations.
icml-2026-spikinglm-towards-fully-spikin.tldr: SpikingLM stabilizes spiking language-model training and restores efficient token competition, reporting lower energy use and strong GLUE performance.

paragraphs: A mathematically correct example can still provide ineffective guidance to a reasoning model. This paper distinguishes strategy usage, meaning that a strategy appears in a successful solution, from strategy executability, meaning that a target model can use that strategy effectively when given it as guidance. The distinction explains why relevant examples can produce unstable improvements.

A controlled comparison of paired human-written and model-generated solutions finds that usage and executability diverge systematically. Human and model strategies have complementary strengths that vary by domain, and which source works better can reverse when strategies become guidance. Selective Strategy Retrieval uses empirical, multi-route, source-aware signals to choose and combine strategies at inference time.

Across mathematical reasoning benchmarks, this framework consistently improves over direct solving, in-context learning, and guidance from only one source. For compact reasoning models, reported accuracy gains reach 13 points on AIME25 and five points on Apex. The findings make the target model's ability to execute a strategy central to selecting guidance, alongside the strategy's mathematical correctness and relevance.
icml-2026-strategy-executability-in-math.tldr: Selective Strategy Retrieval improves mathematical guidance by choosing strategies a target model can effectively execute.

paragraphs: Visual reinforcement learning agents can encounter large changes in appearance that matter little to their task. With sparse rewards, exploration can therefore be distracted by irrelevant variation. TEB ties exploration to a learned representation of behavioral relevance, using a predictive bisimulation metric both to shape that representation and to measure novelty within it.

Sparse rewards can cause degenerate bisimulation metrics to collapse representations, obscuring useful distinctions between states. TEB introduces a predicted reward differential term, with a theoretical account of how it mitigates that collapse. Building on the resulting metric, potential-based exploration bonuses use anchor states to measure relative novelty across the latent space.

Experiments on MetaWorld and Maze2D report stronger exploration and better performance than recent baselines. The central contribution is the coupling between what the agent represents and what it considers worth exploring. Task-relevant distinctions guide the representation, and that same representation guides intrinsic novelty, helping exploration focus on meaningful behavioral differences rather than simply on changing visual observations.
icml-2026-task-aware-exploration-via-a-p.tldr: TEB uses a predictive behavioral metric to learn task-relevant visual representations and guide exploration through latent-space novelty.

paragraphs: Zeroth-order optimization improves a model through function evaluations when backpropagation is unavailable. Existing approaches can require many evaluations or suffer from noisy randomized estimates. Coherent Coordinate Descent offers a deterministic, budget-aware alternative that reuses historical gradient information to reduce the evaluation cost of each optimization step.

The theoretical analysis formalizes gradient coherence and connects the method to block cyclic coordinate descent with warm starts. This explains how older gradient estimates can remain useful computational information. The mechanism achieves constant query complexity per step while maintaining global descent directions. Error bounds also show that larger finite-difference steps can smooth the effective optimization landscape and improve convergence stability.

Experiments use MLP, CNN, and ResNet architectures with up to 270,000 parameters. CoCD improves sample efficiency and convergence loss or accuracy over block cyclic coordinate descent, and is more stable than randomized zeroth-order methods. These results support deterministic, structure-aware updates for the lightweight settings studied. The smoothing analysis also shows why a larger finite-difference step can sometimes help, despite appearing to be a coarser local estimate.
icml-2026-turning-stale-gradients-into-s.tldr: CoCD reuses coherent historical gradients for efficient deterministic zeroth-order optimization and explains how larger finite-difference steps can stabilize learning.

paragraphs: UniFLoW addresses multimodal model adaptation using data distributed across private clients. Clients may hold different modalities, creating architectural incompatibilities, while communicating full updates for billion-scale models is expensive. Low-rank adaptation reduces the update burden, but simply averaging low-rank updates can fail to reproduce the intended global update faithfully.

The framework combines a pretrained language model with a multimodal encoder architecture and an analytical aggregation method called FedA²-LoRA. Modality-specific encoders and a two-stage training strategy integrate heterogeneous inputs while addressing overfitting. The analytical aggregation component targets the inconsistency introduced when combining client-side low-rank updates, allowing fragmented multimodal data to contribute within one federated framework.

Experiments on text, images, and speech demonstrate scalable, communication-efficient fine-tuning with consistent aggregation. FedA²-LoRA achieves state-of-the-art performance relative to existing federated LoRA approaches. The contribution joins two requirements that must work together: accommodating clients with different input types and combining their efficient updates faithfully. This supports the use of otherwise underutilized private data as public training data becomes scarcer.
icml-2026-uniflow-universal-multi-modal-.tldr: UniFLoW combines modality-specific encoders with analytical LoRA aggregation for efficient federated adaptation across text, image, and speech clients.

paragraphs: Vector animation must connect discrete SVG code with continuous-looking motion while preserving editable structure. VAnim represents animation as sparse updates to a persistent SVG document tree. Keeping that structure in place allows the framework to model non-rigid geometric changes while maintaining the identities and relationships of the underlying visual elements.

The sparse-update representation compresses sequence length by more than 9.8 times and mathematically guarantees topological isomorphism and identity persistence. Identification-first motion planning connects text instructions to explicit visual entities. To learn from rendered results despite non-differentiable SVG rendering, the method uses group relative policy optimization with a hybrid reward informed by a video perception encoder.

The authors introduce the SVGAnim-134k benchmark and report substantial improvements over state-of-the-art baselines in semantic alignment and structural validity. Experiments also demonstrate high-fidelity non-rigid deformation without explicit temporal-consistency constraints. The key connection is between a representation that preserves document structure by design and a training signal that assesses the visual consequences of code updates. Both are important for animation that remains structurally usable as vector graphics.
icml-2026-vanim-rendering-aware-sparse-s.tldr: VAnim generates text-controlled SVG animations through sparse updates that preserve structure and learn from rendered visual feedback.

paragraphs: Panoramic editing must respect spherical scene structure. Perspective-based editors do not model that structure directly, and decomposing a panorama into cube faces breaks global consistency. World-Shaper instead works directly in the equirectangular representation, using one panorama-native framework to support five editing operations while accounting for the distortions of that projection.

Its learning strategy handles geometry at several levels. Distortion-aware attention changes cross-attention strength with latitude, while a layered shape loss supervises individual objects' geometry in the output. Progressive curriculum training develops panoramic priors. To obtain paired editing data, a dedicated controllable generator synthesizes objects directly in equirectangular images under user-specified conditions.

Evaluations on the authors' PEBench benchmark report better geometric consistency, editing fidelity, and text controllability than state-of-the-art methods. The contribution combines a representation aligned with the full panorama, training objectives that address its distortion, and scalable construction of paired examples. Together, these components support coherent edits across a 360-degree image while maintaining control through text and a unified editing framework.
icml-2026-world-shaper-a-unified-framewo.tldr: World-Shaper edits panoramas directly in equirectangular space using geometry-aware learning and synthetic paired editing data.
